title: Validity conditions for a phase action
statement: Let $\phi$ be a phase with $\text{main}(\phi)=\text{true}$, and let $s,v,m$ be optional Boolean symbols. The action prescribed by the phase and these symbols writes nothing on the value tape; its mark-tape write is either absent or writes a mark when $v$ is present. If it halts, it emits a symbol. If its next state is a read state for phase $\phi'$, it emits nothing, has $\text{main}(\phi')=\text{true}$, and either does not move the work heads or moves them right when $v$ is present; moreover, whenever $\text{walk}(\phi')$ is false, the current phase is not a walking phase and the work heads do not move. If its next state is a value-tape rewind state for a phase $\phi'$, it emits nothing, has $\text{main}(\phi')=\text{true}$ and $\text{walk}(\phi')=\text{false}$, moves the work heads left, and has $v$ present. If its next state is an append state, it emits nothing, does not move the work heads or write on the mark tape, and the current phase is not a walking phase.
